package_info.package_versions: all versions uploaded by 'Lolip0p' between Jan 7-12, 2023
package_info.why_malicious: All three packages contain a malicious setup.py that executes PowerShell to download and run an info-stealing executable (Oxyz.exe), which further drops additional malware to steal browser data, Discord tokens, and other sensitive information from the developer's system.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Downloads an executable (Oxyz.exe) from a remote server and executes it on the victim's machine.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: setup.py should only handle package installation, not download and execute remote binaries.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal setup.py scripts do not invoke PowerShell to fetch and run executables from the internet.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, setup.py might download dependencies, but never arbitrary executables.
key_indicators: PowerShell invocation from Python setup script

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Oxyz.exe (binary, not shown, but described as info-stealer)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Steals browser information and possibly other sensitive data from the infected system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Oxyz.exe is not a legitimate dependency and is flagged by AV vendors as an info-stealer.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should drop and execute an info-stealing binary.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; legitimate packages do not drop info-stealers.
key_indicators: Executable dropped and run by setup.py

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: SearchProtocolHost.exe (binary, not shown, but described as info-stealer/Discord token stealer)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Collects Discord tokens and other sensitive information, exfiltrates to attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: SearchProtocolHost.exe is not a legitimate system process in this context and is flagged as malicious.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should drop and execute a Discord token stealer.
key_indicators: Suspiciously named executable mimicking Windows process

attack_chain.action: User installs the malicious PyPI package, triggering setup.py.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote download and execution of Oxyz.exe

attack_chain.action: setup.py downloads and executes Oxyz.exe via PowerShell.

attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of info-stealer and Discord token stealer

attack_chain.action: SearchProtocolHost.exe collects browser data, Discord tokens, and exfiltrates to attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen credentials and data

behavioral_signatures: setup.py invoking PowerShell or other shell commands to download and execute remote binaries
Installation-time network connections to suspicious or non-standard domains
Dropped executables with names mimicking Windows system processes (e.g., SearchProtocolHost.exe)
Unexpected process creation from Python package installation
file_indicators: setup.py containing os.system or subprocess calls to PowerShell
Presence of Oxyz.exe, update.exe, or SearchProtocolHost.exe in temp directories
Unusual files in AppData\Local\Temp with random directory names
network_indicators: HTTP requests to suspicious domains (e.g., URLs hosting Oxyz.exe)
Outbound connections immediately after package installation
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Python package installations for setup.py scripts that invoke shell commands, especially those that download and execute remote files. Flag any package that drops executables in user directories or temp folders. Use endpoint security to detect known info-stealer binaries (Oxyz.exe, SearchProtocolHost.exe) and monitor for suspicious network activity following package installation.
